title: Deek Watson's diamond ring and burning five-dollar bills
summary: Kenney and Watson wore big diamond rings that flashed in the spotlight, and Watson lit cigars with five-dollar bills.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Well, you said, too, that I think it was Deak Watson who was quite a show-off.

Oh, yeah-yeah-yeah. Bill Kenney would be singing the lead at the microphone, and they had a big... Both of them had five-carat diamond rings on. And Bill Kenney would be waving his hand and singing in the

spotlight, and then the spotlight hit the diamond ring, and oh, it would splurge all over the theatre. So he would be singin' and wavin' his hands in the spotlight, and Deak would edge over in front of him and wave his ring up and down like he's wavin' at somebody goodbye.
Oh, they was... I don't know, they was just something else. And the people loved it. The people loved it, believe me. They were laughing all the way to the bank.
Was it Deak Watson who used to light up his cigar in a special way.
Well, now, I can't say that. No, no, I am not saying that. He might not be dead. They might put him in jail!

Well, I don't know. Funny things happen, you know. I don't know whether he did or not, but he sure did... He used to light his cigar with five-dollar bills. He'd light up a five-dollar bill and light his cigar with it. He had little regard for money, for the value of it. Let them control the wealth of the country, they'd never have no more depressions. Yes, indeed, there would never be no more depressions. They'd see that the money gets...
Gets spread around. And it would be spread
